prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Houston, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1256; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: This is the adjuster following up on your claim from the rear-end collision in Houston. Is it all right if I record this statement?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Thank you. Please state where you were and what you were doing when the collision happened.

A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road in Houston, waiting to turn. I had my foot on the brake and my car was completely still.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before it hit you?

A: Not really. I checked my mirror a moment before, and it looked like the car behind me was slowing down. The next thing I knew there was a hard jolt from behind.

Q: How fast do you think the other car was going when it made contact?

A: It didn't feel very fast, but it was enough to push me forward into the car in front of me. I'd guess it was moderate speed, not a crawl.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle and speak with the other driver?

A: I did. He apologized and said he had looked down at his phone for a second. We exchanged information, and an officer came to write up a report.

Q: Did you have any injuries at the scene?

A: I didn't feel much right away. Over the next day my neck got stiff and sore, and by the following morning I had trouble turning my head to the left. My neck and upper shoulders ache, and I've had a headache most days.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or received any treatment since?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care that same week. They diagnosed a neck strain, gave me muscle relaxers, and told me to do gentle stretching and use ice. I've been going to physical therapy twice a week since then.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Only that I've missed a few days of work because of the pain, and I'd like the claim to reflect that. Thank you for listening.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
